title: HB2103 (2019-2020 Regular): Simplifying firearms regulations.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States public data converted to LegiScan layout (gun-policy Stage 5, Washington); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Washington Legislature text (Introduced, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/Biennium/2019-20/Htm/Bills/House%20Bills/2103.htm, downloaded directly)
provenance.note: Introduced version. Quotes are the bill's resulting text with struck words left out; the struck text in Sec. 4 includes the loaded-pistol-in-vehicle ban and the unloaded-pistol-in-vehicle lock rule, and in Sec. 21 the under-21 purchase and possession limits (both repealed in effect). Sec. 10 also strikes the 60-day extended wait for some pistol buyers and the separate wait for semiautomatic assault rifles. Sec. 24 repeals 20 sections; only items (12)-(15) are quoted, the others (RCW 9.41.065, .080, .094, .097, .0975, .114, .129, .137, .139, .173, .175, 36.28A.400-.420, 43.43.823) are not. Sec. 6 (RCW 9.41.070), Secs. 8, 9, 11-20, 22-23 not quoted; Sec. 23 re-ranks gun offences in RCW 9.94A.515 and drops bump-fire stock and short-barreled firearm items from some crime names. Sec. 2 findings cite Wash. Const. art. I sec. 24 and the Second Amendment as legislative findings. Effective July 1, 2019 with emergency clause (Sec. 26). Large file; read via grep and targeted sections.

Sec. 4 (RCW 9.41.050): (2) A person may carry a loaded pistol in a vehicle for the purpose of self-defense, prevention of a felony crime, or protection of the public.
Sec. 10 (RCW 9.41.092): Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, a licensed dealer must deliver any firearm to a purchaser or transferee once the earlier of the following occurs: (1) The results of all required background checks are known and the purchaser or transferee is not prohibited from owning or possessing a firearm under federal or state law; or (2) Ten business days have elapsed from the date the licensed dealer requested the background check.
Sec. 21 (RCW 9.41.240): (1) A person over seventeen years of age may purchase a firearm in accordance with federal law.
Sec. 21 (RCW 9.41.240): (2) A person over seventeen years of age may possess a firearm in any place and circumstance where it is legal according to state law.
Sec. 7 (RCW 9.41.073): (1)(a) A person licensed to carry a pistol in a state other than this state is authorized to carry a concealed pistol in this state if: (i) The licensing state does not issue concealed pistol licenses to persons under twenty-one years of age; and (ii) The licensing state requires mandatory fingerprint-based background checks of criminal history.
